title: A Orbit for the Protocol
premise: Noor Lockridge, a terraformer on the half-built colony of Meridian's Rest, tends an orbital garden for settlers who haven't arrived yet, running supply routes between two colonies severed by a decades-old diplomatic rupture. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream — a night of fire in the settlement that was supposedly never harmed — Noor discovers her own suppressed memories match it, and that the 'accident' both governments erased was a massacre covered up to preserve their fragile peace. As she digs, she finds the dream is being broadcast deliberately by a dying survivor hiding in the garden's life-support systems, and that the children are the only witnesses the truth has left. To prove what happened, Noor must betray the found family who raised her and risk severing the route that keeps Meridian's Rest alive; in the end she broadcasts the survivors' testimony to both worlds at once, forcing a reckoning that costs her the garden but wins the children — and the dead — a place in the record.
about_author: Astrid Coldharbour spent nine years as a hydroponics technician in high-latitude research stations before turning to fiction, and her prose still smells faintly of grow-lights and recycled air. She writes about people who keep things alive in places built to be forgotten.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Noor pilots the supply run between Meridian's Rest and its estranged sister colony Vantage, tending seedlings destined for unborn settlers. POV: Noor. Establishes her solitary devotion to the garden and the silence between the two worlds. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: Children of the Quiet Season
chapters.summary: Back on the ground, Noor teaches the colony's children botany in the greenhouse dome. Seven-year-old Idris describes a recurring dream: burning dormitories, a voice counting names. Other children chime in — same dream, same details. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: unease blooming under warmth.

chapters.title: Records Say Otherwise
chapters.summary: Noor searches the colony archive for the incident Idris described and finds only a benign log: a systems fault, no casualties, sealed by joint decree. Administrator Sefa Okonkwo gently warns her off. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: What the Garden Remembers
chapters.summary: Working the night shift, Noor hears a signal threaded through the irrigation telemetry — a patterned pulse, almost like breathing. It resolves into fragments of audio: screaming, then a woman reciting names. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: dread and wonder entangled.

chapters.title: Sefa's Kindness
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Sefa's POV: how she took orphaned Noor in after her parents' transport failed, and why she believes some truths must stay buried for the colonies' fragile truce to hold. Emotional beat: love as a form of concealment.

chapters.title: The Dream Spreads
chapters.summary: Fourteen children now share the dream, and two have begun sleepwalking toward the sealed old habitat ring. The colony doctor, Anselm Reyes, confides he dreamed it too — before the children were born. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay past.

chapters.title: Into the Sealed Ring
chapters.summary: Noor breaks into the decommissioned habitat and finds scorch patterns the official record denies, plus a jury-rigged transmitter wired into the garden's uplink. Someone has been living here. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your home is a crime scene.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Walls
chapters.summary: Noor confronts the transmitter's keeper: Yara Vance, officially listed among the accident's zero casualties, surviving on scavenged rations for nineteen years. Yara has been broadcasting the dream into the children's shared neural mesh, unable to stop. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized into testimony.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names
chapters.summary: Yara recounts the massacre: Vantage security forces killed nineteen colonists during an evacuation dispute, and both governments buried it to protect the trade corridor. Noor realizes her parents were on that list. POV: Yara, with Noor present. Emotional beat: grief arriving late but whole.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Noor weighs exposing the truth against the consequences: Vantage will cut the supply route, and Meridian's Rest cannot survive a year without it. Sefa discovers her archive breach. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: the cost of every choice made visible.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Daughter
chapters.summary: Sefa confronts Noor, not with anger but with fear, revealing she signed the cover-up to secure adoption rights for massacre orphans — including Noor. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: betrayal and protection revealed as the same act.

chapters.title: The Children Vote
chapters.summary: Idris and the older children, having pieced together the adults' evasions, demand to meet the woman in their dreams. Noor must decide whether they are victims of Yara's broadcast or its intended jurors. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: agency passing to the next generation.

chapters.title: Meeting in the Burned Wing
chapters.summary: Noor smuggles the children into the sealed ring. Yara tells them the truth plainly; Idris asks the question no adult dared: 'Who said we had to choose between peace and memory?' POV: Idris. Emotional beat: innocence sharpening into moral clarity.

chapters.title: Vantage Hears Something
chapters.summary: A Vantage patrol detects anomalous transmissions from Meridian's Rest. The route is suspended pending inspection, and an investigator, Captain Odile Ferran, arrives — a former security officer whose unit may have been there that night. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: the machinery of denial grinding closer.

chapters.title: The Investigator's Doubt
chapters.summary: Odile audits the colony and interviews Noor, sensing evasion. Alone, she checks her own service records and finds a nineteen-day gap exactly matching the incident date. POV: Odile. Emotional beat: a loyal soldier's foundation tilting.

chapters.title: Raid on the Garden
chapters.summary: Odile's sweep closes in on Yara's hideout. Noor moves Yara through the garden's maintenance shafts while the children create diversions; Sefa, forced to choose, misdirects the search party. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other under pressure.

chapters.title: Yara Failing
chapters.summary: Hidden in the seed vault, Yara's radiation exposure from nineteen years in the ring becomes terminal. She entrusts Noor with the full testimony — names, footage, the order that came from Vantage command — and asks not for vindication but for the children to remember freely. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: mortality compressing time.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Decision
chapters.summary: Noor plans to transmit the testimony on the emergency band to both colonies simultaneously during the next supply window. Sefa offers to help, accepting her own reckoning; Odile, having found the gap in her records, arrives not to arrest but to corroborate. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: allies assembling from unlikely quarters.

chapters.title: Severance
chapters.summary: Vantage, tipped off, cuts the route early and demands Yara's surrender. With the colony's oxygen reserves tied to the garden grid, Noor must broadcast from the garden itself, knowing the transmission will burn out the systems keeping it alive. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: sacrifice made concrete and irreversible.

chapters.title: Nineteen Names, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: Climax: Noor reads the testimony live to both worlds while the garden's lights die section by section around her. The children join in over the open channel, speaking the names they learned in dreams. Odile confirms the orders on-record. Vantage's command structure fractures publicly. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: truth as an act of endurance.

chapters.title: After the Silence Breaks
chapters.summary: Inquiry convened jointly; Sefa testifies to her part; the route reopens under new terms requiring shared archives. Yara dies with her name restored to the living record, mourned publicly. Noor, stripped of her terraformer post, is unmoored. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: A Garden for People Not Yet Born
chapters.summary: A year later, the children build a memorial grove in the reopened ring, planting seeds Noor saved from the burned-out vault. Offered leadership of the new joint colony, Noor instead chooses to teach — and to finally grieve her parents by name. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.
